themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Central Harlem is experiencing a spike in dead animal complaints with 3 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 0.5 per week—a 500% increase (z-score: 5.0)—signaling potential public health and sanitation infrastructure failures.
evidence: 3 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0, severity: high)
This represents a 500% spike in a category rarely reported
Spike occurred concurrent with warm weather onset (early May data context)
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Sanitation Department and local residents about disposal protocols and any citywide staffing shortages
Document specific locations and conditions; investigate whether related illegal dumping or rodent population issues underlie the spike

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints tripled THIS WEEK to 3 reports versus a baseline of 1.0 per week (200% spike, z-score: 4.0), suggesting potential environmental code violations or construction-related damage in the district.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.0, severity: high)
Spike coincides with 482 DOB building permit filings in district (411 alterations alone), suggesting construction-related damage
Three active ULURP applications in pipeline may indicate ongoing development pressure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits filed in last 1-2 weeks with tree damage complaint locations to identify construction-caused violations
Interview Parks Department and Environmental Health advocates about enforcement and contractor accountability

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked dramatically 3 weeks ago to 32 reports versus a 7.8 weekly average (313% increase, z-score: 5.33, severity: high)—though this spike may be subsiding, the scale signals potential infrastructure crisis.
evidence: 32 water system complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.33, severity: high)
Represents 313% spike in critical infrastructure category
Contextually linked to recent City Limits reporting on NYCHA elevator/building infrastructure delays in East Harlem (adjacent to Central Harlem)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether spike reflects water main breaks, DEP pressure issues, or NYCHA/public housing building failures; obtain DEP incident logs
Interview affected residents and property managers; cross-check if complaints concentrated in specific buildings or neighborhoods within CD110

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Disorder
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped 269% last week to 6 reports versus a 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.41)—indicating potential Uber/Lyft congestion, illegal parking, or traffic safety issues emerging in Central Harlem.
evidence: 6 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.41, severity: high)
Represents 269% spike in a previously low-volume complaint category
District has sustained illegal parking complaints (1,350 over 90 days), suggesting underlying vehicle/congestion pressure
reporting_angles: Map where for-hire vehicles are clustering; interview TLC enforcement and residents about specific pain points (double-parking, blocking hydrants, noise)
Investigate whether spike correlates with event venues, subway disruptions, or shift in gig driver behavior post-rate changes

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks spiked 344% last week to 5 reports versus a 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.68), suggesting overcrowding, events, or enforcement gaps as weather warms heading into summer.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.68, severity: high)
Represents 344% spike coinciding with onset of warm weather and outdoor gathering season
Contextually tied to CB budget requests for park facilities and maintenance (recurring annual ask)
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints (e.g., Marcus Garvey, Mount Morris, St. Nicholas); interview Parks Enforcement and neighbors
Explore whether spike reflects permitted events, unpermitted gatherings, or enforcement resource gaps
